4 اغنّ said of a man, He made one to hear his ↓ غُنَّة , i. e. soft, or gentle, plaintive, and melodious, voice, in singing. (Har p. 645.) ―
-b2- اغنّ الذُّبَابُ The flies made a sound [or humming]. (K.) ―
-b3- اغنّ الوَادِى (tropical:) The valley had in it the sound [or humming] of flies, [or resounded therewith,] being abundant in herbs, or herbage: (S:) or abounded with trees; as also ↓ غَنَّ . (K, TA.) ―
-b4- اغنّت الأَرْض (assumed tropical:) The land had its herbs, or herbage, tall, full-grown, or of full height, and in blossom. (TA.) ―
-b5- اغنّ النَّخْلُ (tropical:) The palm-trees attained to maturity; as also ↓ غَنَّ . (K, TA.) ―
-b6- And اغنّ السِّقَآءُ (tropical:) The skin became filled (S, K, TA) with water. (S, TA.) ＝
-A2- And [it is also trans.:] one says, اغنّ ٱللّٰهُ غُصْنَهُ (tropical:) God made its branch beautiful and bright. (K, TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
